--- title: dictionary --- ```python dictionary(dataset, scale=None, ref=None) ``` The variable dictionary of a dataset, one row per column. ## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} | Name | Type | Description | Default | |---------|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------|------------| | dataset | str | Dataset id (see ``geo.datasets()``) | _required_ | | scale | str \| None | The resource's scale (default: the dataset's native scale) | `None` | ## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns} | Name | Type | Description | |--------|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | | pandas.DataFrame | Columns ``variable``, ``label`` (the field's ``title``, a readable name for plot axes and legends), ``description`` (how it was built), ``unit``, ``role`` (id, time, source_key or variable), ``aggregation`` (the rule ``geo.aggregate`` uses), ``source`` and ``reference_years`` (the actual years behind each stored year, e.g. ``"2012: 2008; 2024: 2023"``, when they differ). | ## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example} ```python !pip install -q geo4bolivia import geo4bolivia as geo import plotly.express as px d = geo.dictionary("sdg03") display(d[["variable", "label", "unit", "aggregation", "reference_years"]]) ``` ::: {#d09205e3 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
